Get district-level police crime statistics

Source: R/pks_get.R
pks_get.Rd

Downloads the district (Kreis) tables of the German Police Crime Statistics (PKS) from a versioned data release, as published by the Bundeskriminalamt or harmonized to one territorial boundary and offence classification. Files are cached and checked against the SHA-256 checksums of the release manifest.

Usage

pks_get(
  years = NULL,
  offence_keys = NULL,
  harmonize_to = "latest",
  weights = c("population", "area"),
  version = "latest",
  source = c("release", "bka"),
  cache = TRUE
)

Arguments

years

Integer vector of reporting years, or NULL (default) for all years of the release.

offence_keys

Character vector of offence keys (Straftatenschluessel), or NULL (default) for all. For harmonized data these are the harmonized keys listed by pks_offences(); for the data as published, the keys as printed in the BKA tables.

harmonize_to

Target boundary year (Gebietsstand). "latest" (default) is the boundary of the release, read as released; another year harmonizes the data as published with the crosswalk of the release (forward only, so years must not be later than the target); NULL returns the data as published.

weights

Weights for districts that were split: "population" (default) or "area". Ignored for harmonize_to = NULL.

version

Data version such as "2026.1", or "latest" (default).

source

"release" (default) reads a data release. "bka", which will rebuild the spreadsheet years from the original BKA files, is not available yet.

cache

Keep downloaded files in the cache (default TRUE). With FALSE, files go to a temporary directory and are removed with the R session.

Value

A tibble with one row per year, district (ags) and offence key. Columns are described in vignette("pksR"). Attributes: data_version, retrieved_at, boundary_year, weights and source_urls.

See also

Other data: pks_example()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# Total offences, harmonized to the latest boundary
total <- pks_get(offence_keys = "------")

# As published by the BKA, two years
published <- pks_get(years = 2024:2025, harmonize_to = NULL)
}
